title: Consumer Trends 2024-2026
summary: The themes reshaping US consumer demand right now, each with who it hits and how it shows up in a case. Use these to form a hypothesis fast when a client's sales move and the cause isn't operational.

blocks.title: Value, inflation and spending mix
rows: Value-seeking & private label
Store brands hit a record ~$283B in 2025, ~21% of dollar and ~24% of unit sales (PLMA/Circana); growing faster than national brands
CPG brands; grocers win margin
Brand losing share: check private-label price gaps before blaming marketing
Inflation hangover
Annual food price increases have slowed (~2% for groceries in 2025) but price levels stay well above 2020, and restaurant prices keep rising faster
Lower- and middle-income households; QSRs
Traffic down despite stable prices: consumers anchor on pre-2021 prices; value menus and bundles return
K-shaped spending
Top 10% of earners ~half of spending (Moody's, 2025)
Mass-market vs premium brands diverge
Split the customer base by income before forecasting
Experiences over goods
Services are ~69% of US consumer spending (BEA, mid-2026)
Travel, live events, dining vs durable goods
Retailers compete with concerts and trips for discretionary dollars

blocks.title: Health and lifestyle
rows: GLP-1 drugs
~12% of adults were taking a GLP-1 (KFF, late 2025); households with a user cut grocery spend ~5% and savory snacks ~10% (Cornell/Numerator)
Snacks, sweets, fast food, alcohol; helps protein, yogurt, fresh
Snack volume decline: model GLP-1 adoption; consider smaller packs and high-protein lines
Health & wellness
US wellness market ~$500B+, growing ~4-5% a year; most consumers call wellness a priority (McKinsey, 2025)
Food, beverage, fitness, supplements, beauty
Reposition products on protein, gut health, sleep, functional benefits
Younger adults drinking less
Only ~54% of adults drink, a record low; ~50% of 18-34s (Gallup, 2025)
Beer, wine, spirits; bars
Alcohol volume decline is structural; growth in non-alcoholic and premium 'drink less, better'

blocks.title: Channels and digital
rows: Convenience & delivery
E-commerce ~17% of retail sales (Q2 2026, Census); delivery and pickup are routine for many households
Grocers, restaurants, pharmacies
Fees, basket size and density decide profitability
Subscriptions & fatigue
Households average ~4 paid streaming services at ~$69/month; ~39% canceled one in six months (Deloitte, 2025)
Streaming, meal kits, software, memberships
Churn-and-return; ad-supported tiers and bundles to hold users
Social commerce
US social commerce ~$87B in 2025, TikTok Shop ~20% of it (eMarketer)
Beauty, fashion, small brands
Creator-led launches; live shopping; watch return rates and margins
AI in shopping
Generative AI traffic to US retail sites rose several-fold in the 2025 holidays and converted better than other traffic (Adobe)
Retailers, brands, search ads
Be visible in AI answers; product data quality becomes marketing

blocks.title: Sustainability: say vs do
blocks.body: Surveys consistently show many shoppers say they prefer sustainable products and would pay more, but at the shelf price and convenience usually win, especially for lower-income households. Evidence is mixed rather than zero: a McKinsey-NielsenIQ study found products with ESG claims grew ~28% vs ~20% for others over 2017-2022. Durable takeaway: sustainability works best as a tie-breaker at near-parity price, not as a premium most buyers will pay.

blocks.title: Start with the trend checklist
blocks.body: When a consumer client's numbers move, run a quick external scan before diving into operations: income segment (K-shape), price gap to private label, channel shift to online/social, health trends (GLP-1, alcohol), and seasonality. Naming one or two relevant trends with a test you'd run sounds senior.

blocks.title: Trends are uneven
blocks.body: Don't apply a national trend uniformly. GLP-1 use, delivery adoption and social shopping vary by age, income and geography. Ask 'how much of this client's customer base is exposed?' and size the effect, rather than treating any trend as a market-wide shock.

blocks.title: Quick reads on each trend for interviews
items: Trading down is selective: shoppers cut in staples while keeping a few treats ('lipstick effect').
BNPL and credit help sustain spending for stretched households but add risk if delinquencies rise.
GLP-1 effects concentrate in higher-income households, where grocery cuts exceed 8% (Cornell).
Ad-supported streaming tiers now reach most subscribers, shifting economics toward advertising.
AI shopping assistants raise the bar on product data, reviews and price transparency.

in_a_case: Snack maker's volumes falling: test GLP-1 adoption among core buyers and private-label substitution before cutting marketing spend.
Casual-dining traffic decline: inflation hangover plus lower-income pullback; value bundles and loyalty offers vs further price increases.
Beer company growth strategy: structural decline in young-adult drinking points to non-alcoholic, low-ABV and adjacent categories.
Streaming platform profitability: model churn-and-return and ad-tier mix rather than a fixed subscriber lifetime.
A DTC beauty brand: social commerce and creators as an acquisition channel, with attention to returns and platform fees.

flashcards.back: ~21% of dollar sales, ~24% of units; record ~$283B (PLMA/Circana).
